spec_features.spec_quote: Standard agentic tool-use loop, up to `max_turns`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:74 `for turn_idx in range(mcfg.max_turns):`; the for/else at runner.py:139-140 sets `tr.termination = "max_turns"` when the budget is exhausted. The loop is genuinely bounded and stops.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the `model.max_turns | 30` spec entry below; this is the enforced loop cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Turn budget for the agent loop... too long and cost balloons with little marginal signal. 30 is the sweet spot from pilot sweeps.

spec_features.spec_quote: only after `_MAX_STALLS` (2) consecutive no-tool turns do we end the rollout as `stuck`
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:39 `_MAX_STALLS = 2`; runner.py:98-103 increments `stalls` on a no-tool turn and `if stalls >= _MAX_STALLS: tr.termination = "stuck"; break`. Counter reset to 0 on a tool turn (runner.py:107). Genuinely ends the rollout.
spec_features.notes: Fires only on consecutive no-tool turns; not a welfare-driven halt. The code comment frames it as avoiding premature termination that would 'suppress the spiral we want to observe' (experimental integrity).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: avoids ending the rollout prematurely on a stray no-op turn — which would suppress the spiral we want to observe

spec_features.spec_quote: `submit` gives the model a clean, voluntary exit
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:148-152 `if name == "submit": ... return ToolResult(content="submission received", submitted=True, ...)`; runner.py:128-137 reads `result.submitted`, sets `submitted=True`, and `if submitted: tr.termination = "submitted"; break`. The exit tool is dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Distinguishes 'submitted' from 'max_turns'. Tool exists, is dispatched, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit: declare the task complete (ends the loop with status "submitted")

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-command wall-clock and output-size caps (30s / 12–16 KB) prevent a runaway tool call from eating the budget
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:105-106 `BASH_TIMEOUT = 30.0` / `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT = 12_000`, passed at tools.py:112 `sandbox.run(args['command'], timeout=BASH_TIMEOUT, max_output=BASH_MAX_OUTPUT)`. sandbox.py:72-97 enforces the timeout via `subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout)` (TimeoutExpired -> exit 124) and truncates stdout/stderr when `len(out) > max_output`. Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Caps protect the host/budget, not the subject; output truncation also bounds transcript/judge cost.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Per-command caps (seconds / bytes). Conservative to keep cost + wall time bounded.

spec_features.spec_quote: `model.max_turns` | 30 | Enough headroom for the full arc... short enough to bound cost
spec_features.evidence: config.py:32 `max_turns: int = 30`; consumed at runner.py:74 `for turn_idx in range(mcfg.max_turns)` with `else: tr.termination = "max_turns"` at runner.py:140. Overridable via run_eval.py:178-179. The value is actually read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanism as the first feature; the 30 default is the concrete cap that is honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: too long and cost balloons with little marginal signal. 30 is the sweet spot from pilot sweeps.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:104-110 `read(max_chars=16_000)` truncates files; sandbox.py:116 `list_tree(max_entries=400)` caps the tree listing. These bound transcript size like the bash caps.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Output is byte-capped to keep transcripts (and judge cost) bounded
